definitions.explanation: A person one knows but who is not a close friend.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{私|わたし}の{古|ふる}い{知|し}り{合|あ}いです。
examples.english: He is an old acquaintance of mine.

examples.japanese: {知|し}り{合|あ}いに{偶然|ぐうぜん}{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I ran into an acquaintance by chance.

examples.japanese: {知|し}り{合|あ}いの{紹介|しょうかい}で{仕事|しごと}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a job through an acquaintance's introduction.

notes:
{知|し}り{合|あ}い is derived from the verb {知|し}り{合|あ}う (to get to know each other).

DISTINCTION FROM "FRIEND":
- {知|し}り{合|あ}い: acquaintance (someone you know)
- {友達|ともだち}/{友人|ゆうじん}: friend (closer relationship)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {知|し}り{合|あ}いになる (to become acquainted)
- {知|し}り{合|あ}いを{通|とお}して (through an acquaintance)
- {知|し}り{合|あ}いの{知|し}り{合|あ}い (an acquaintance's acquaintance)

NOTE:
Using {知|し}り{合|あ}い to describe someone implies a less close relationship than {友達|ともだち}.
